otherwise—6 months.
Matters to which nominated ART Intelligence and Security member must have regard
In deciding whether to issue an international production order under subclause (2), the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member must have regard to the following matters:
in the case of an application for an international production order that is in respect of one or more individual transmission services:

to what extent methods of carrying out the Organisation’s function of obtaining intelligence relating to security (so far as carrying out that function relates to the target) that are less intrusive than accessing, under such an order, communications being carried by those individual transmission services have been used by, or are available to, the Organisation; and

how much the use of such methods would be likely to assist the Organisation in carrying out its function of obtaining intelligence relating to security (so far as carrying out that function relates to the target); and

how much the use of such methods would be likely to prejudice the Organisation in carrying out its function of obtaining intelligence relating to security (so far as carrying out that function relates to the target), whether because of delay or for any other reason; and
such other matters (if any) as the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member considers relevant;
in the case of an application for an international production order that is in respect of one or more individual message/call application services:

to what extent methods of carrying out the Organisation’s function of obtaining intelligence relating to security (so far as carrying out that function relates to the target) that are less intrusive than accessing, under such an order, messages sent or received, voice calls made or received, or video calls made or received, using those individual message/call application services have been used by, or are available to, the Organisation; and

how much the use of such methods would be likely to assist the Organisation in carrying out its function of obtaining intelligence relating to security (so far as carrying out that function relates to the target); and

how much the use of such methods would be likely to prejudice the Organisation in carrying out its function of obtaining intelligence relating to security (so far as carrying out that function relates to the target), whether because of delay or for any other reason; and
such other matters (if any) as the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member considers relevant.
Note: For target, see subclause (8).
Restriction on issuing order

The nominated ART Intelligence and Security member must not issue an international production order under subclause (2) in a case where subparagraph (2)(e)(ii) applies unless the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member is satisfied that:

the Organisation has exhausted all other practicable methods of identifying the individual transmission services used, or likely to be used, by the other person mentioned in subparagraph (2)(e)(ii); or

interception (as permitted under an international production order) of communications carried by individual transmission services used or likely to be used by that other person would not otherwise be possible.

The nominated ART Intelligence and Security member must not issue an international production order under subclause (2) in a case where subparagraph (2)(f)(ii) applies unless the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member is satisfied that:

the Organisation has exhausted all other practicable methods of identifying the individual message/call application services used, or likely to be used, by the other person mentioned in subparagraph (2)(f)(ii); or

interception (as permitted under an international production order) of messages sent or received, voice calls made or received, or video calls made or received, using individual message/call application services used or likely to be used by that other person would not otherwise be possible.
Copying stored communications
If an international production order issued under subclause (2) directs a prescribed communications provider to intercept communications, messages, voice calls or video calls:
the prescribed communications provider may comply with the order by copying stored communications that consist of the communications, messages, voice calls or video calls; and
a copy of a stored communication made for that purpose is taken to be a communication, message, voice call or video call (as the case may be) intercepted under the international production order.
Target
(8) For the purposes of this clause, target means:
if subparagraph (2)(e)(i) or (f)(i) applies—the person referred to in that subparagraph; or
if subparagraph (2)(e)(ii) or (f)(ii) applies—the other person referred to in that subparagraph; or
if subparagraph (2)(e)(iii) or (f)(iii) applies—the purposes referred to in that subparagraph.
Scope
This clause applies to an international production order issued under clause 89.
Content
The order must be signed by the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member who issued it.
The order must set out the following:
the date on which the order was issued;
the name of the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed;
the name of the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order;
the applicable telecommunications identifiers:
in the case of an order that is in respect of one or more individual transmission services—to which those individual transmission services relate; or
in the case of an order that is in respect of one or more individual message/call application services—to which those individual message/call application services relate.
If the order directs a prescribed communications provider to intercept communications, the order may require the provider to:
intercept those communications in a specified way; and
make those intercepted communications available to the Organisation in a specified way.
A requirement under subclause (4) may:
require that intercepted communications be made available to the Organisation directly; or
require that intercepted communications be made available to the Organisation indirectly via the Australian Designated Authority.
If the order directs a prescribed communications provider to intercept messages, voice calls or video calls, the order may require the provider to:
intercept those messages, voice calls or video calls in a specified way; and
make those intercepted messages, voice calls or video calls available to the Organisation in a specified way.
A requirement under subclause (6) may:
require that intercepted messages, voice calls or video calls be made available to the Organisation directly; or
require that intercepted messages, voice calls or video calls be made available to the Organisation indirectly via the Australian Designated Authority.

If the order directs a prescribed communications provider to disclose telecommunications data to the Organisation, the order may require the provider to disclose that data to the Organisation in a specified way.
A requirement under subclause (8) may:
require that the telecommunications data be disclosed to the Organisation directly; or
require that the telecommunications data be disclosed to the Organisation indirectly via the Australian Designated Authority.
For the purposes of this clause, a specified way may deal with matters of timing.
Example: A requirement under subclause (4) may require that an intercepted communication be made available to the Organisation within 30 minutes after the communication was completed.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Issue of further international production order

content.p: If:
(a) an international production order (the original order) was issued under clause 89; and
the original order was in respect of one or more individual transmission services; and
the original order was directed to a prescribed communications provider;
this Schedule does not prevent the issue of a further international production order under clause 89 that is:
in respect of any or all of those services; and
directed to the provider;

so long as the period specified in the further order for the purposes of subparagraph 89(2)(i)(i) of this Schedule begins after the end of the period specified in the original order for the purposes of that subparagraph.
If:
(a) an international production order (the original order) was issued under clause 89; and
the original order was in respect of one or more individual message/call application services; and
the original order was directed to a prescribed communications provider;
this Schedule does not prevent the issue of a further international production order under clause 89 that is:
in respect of any or all of those services; and
directed to the provider;

so long as the period specified in the further order for the purposes of subparagraph 89(2)(j)(i) of this Schedule begins after the end of the period specified in the original order for the purposes of that subparagraph.

hcontainer.name: division
hcontainer.heading: International production orders relating to stored communications: national security

content.p: Subdivision A—Applications

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Application for international production order—national security

content.p: The Organisation may apply to a nominated ART Intelligence and Security member for an international production order under clause 98 that:
is in respect of a particular person; and
is directed to a prescribed communications provider.
The application must nominate a designated international agreement.
The application must be made on the Organisation’s behalf by:
the Director-General of Security; or
a Deputy Director-General of Security; or
a senior position-holder in relation to whom an authorisation is in force under subclause (4).

The Director-General of Security may authorise in writing, for the purposes of subclause (3), senior position-holders who, or classes of senior position-holders who, are entitled under subclause (1) to make applications on the Organisation’s behalf.
Attorney-General’s consent to the making of an application
The Organisation must not make an application under subclause (1) unless the Attorney-General has consented to the making of the application.

The Attorney-General must not consent to the making of an application under subclause (1) for an international production order that is in respect of a particular person unless the Attorney-General is satisfied that:
there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that the person is engaged in, or is likely to engage in, activities prejudicial to security; and

information that would be likely to be obtained by making a copy, under an international production order issued in response to the application, of the stored communications covered by the application would be likely to assist the Organisation in carrying out its function of obtaining intelligence relating to security.
Form of Attorney-General’s consent to the making of an application
Subject to subclause (8), a consent given by the Attorney-General under subclause (5) must be in writing.

If the person who proposes to make an application under subclause (1) on the Organisation’s behalf thinks it necessary, because of urgent circumstances, for the Attorney-General to consent orally to the making of the application:
the person may request the Attorney-General to consent orally to the making of the application; and
if the person makes such a request—the Attorney-General may consent orally to the making of the application.
Note: See also clause 17A (urgent circumstances).

At the same time as a request is made by a person under subclause (8), the person must inform the Attorney-General of the particulars of the urgent circumstances because of which the person thought it necessary for the Attorney-General to consent orally to the making of the application concerned.
If, in response to a request made by a person under subclause (8), the Attorney-General consents orally to the making of an application, the person must:
give the Attorney-General a written report that sets out:
particulars of the urgent circumstances because of which the person thought it necessary for the Attorney-General to consent orally; and
whether the application was granted, withdrawn or refused; and
do so within 3 working days after the day on which the application was granted, withdrawn or refused.
If, in response to a request made by a person under subclause (8), the Attorney-General consents orally to the making of an application, the Organisation must:
give the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security a copy of the relevant report under subclause (9); and
do so within 3 working days after the day on which the application was granted, withdrawn or refused.
An application under clause 92 must be in writing.

If the person making an application under clause 92 for an international production order on the Organisation’s behalf thinks it necessary, because of urgent circumstances, to make the application by telephone, the person may make the application by telephone.
Note: See also clause 17A (urgent circumstances) and clause 172 (action required).
An application under clause 92 must, if it is in writing, set out:
a statement to the effect that the application is made by the Organisation; and
the name of the person making the application on the Organisation’s behalf.
An application under clause 92 must, if it is in writing, be accompanied by an affidavit complying with this clause.
The affidavit must set out the facts and other grounds on which the application is based.

Despite subclause (1), a written application may be accompanied by 2 or more affidavits that together set out each matter that, apart from this subclause, this clause would have required an affidavit accompanying the application to set out.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Information to be given on telephone application

content.p: The information given to a nominated ART Intelligence and Security member in connection with a telephone application under clause 92 to the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member:
must include particulars of the urgent circumstances because of which the person making the application on the Organisation’s behalf thinks it necessary to make the application by telephone; and
must include each matter that, if the application had been made in writing, clause 94 or 95 would have required the application, or an affidavit accompanying it, to set out; and
must be given orally or in writing, as the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member directs.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Giving further information to nominated ART Intelligence and Security member

content.p: A nominated ART Intelligence and Security member may require further information to be given in connection with an application under clause 92 to the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member for an international production order.
The further information:
must be given on oath if the application was made in writing; and
must be given orally or otherwise, as the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member directs.
Subdivision B—International production orders relating to stored communications

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Issue of international production order—national security

content.p: Scope
This clause applies if the Organisation applies, under clause 92, to a nominated ART Intelligence and Security member for an international production order that:
(a) is in respect of a particular person (the relevant person); and
is directed to a prescribed communications provider.
Issue of international production order

If the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member is satisfied, on the basis of the information given to the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member under this Division in connection with the application, that:
there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that the relevant person is engaged in, or is likely to engage in, activities prejudicial to security; and
there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that the prescribed communications provider holds any of the following stored communications:
stored communications that consist of communications that the relevant person has made using a telecommunications network owned or operated by the prescribed communications provider;

stored communications that consist of communications that another person has made using a telecommunications network owned or operated by the prescribed communications provider, and for which the relevant person is the intended recipient;
stored communications that consist of communications that the relevant person has made using a transmission service supplied by the prescribed communications provider;

stored communications that consist of communications that another person has made using a transmission service supplied by the prescribed communications provider, and for which the relevant person is the intended recipient;
stored communications that consist of messages that the relevant person has sent or received using a message/call application service provided by the prescribed communications provider;

stored communications that consist of recordings of voice calls that the relevant person has made or received using a message/call application service provided by the prescribed communications provider;

stored communications that consist of recordings of video calls that the relevant person has made or received using a message/call application service provided by the prescribed communications provider;
stored communications that consist of material that the relevant person has uploaded for storage or back-up by a storage/back-up service provided by the prescribed communications provider;
stored communications that consist of material that the relevant person has posted to a general electronic content service provided by the prescribed communications provider; and

the person who made the application on behalf of the Organisation reasonably suspects that the prescribed communications provider is based in, or operates in, a foreign country that is a party to the designated international agreement nominated in the application; and
Subdivision A has been complied with in relation to the application; and
in the case of a telephone application—because of urgent circumstances, it was necessary to make the application by telephone; and

information that would be likely to be obtained by making a copy, under an order issued under this clause, of the stored communications would be likely to assist the Organisation in carrying out its function of obtaining intelligence relating to security;
the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member may issue an order (to be known as an international production order) directing the prescribed communications provider to:
make a copy of any such stored communications; and
make the copy available to the Organisation; and
if the stored communications consist of communications carried by an individual transmission service—disclose to the Organisation:
specified telecommunications data that relates to those communications; and
specified telecommunications data that relates to the individual transmission service; and
if the stored communications consist of messages sent or received using an individual message/call application service—disclose to the Organisation:
specified telecommunications data that relates to those messages; and
specified telecommunications data that relates to the individual message/call application service; and
if the stored communications consist of recordings of voice calls made or received using an individual message/call application service—disclose to the Organisation:
specified telecommunications data that relates to those voice calls; and
specified telecommunications data that relates to the individual message/call application service; and
if the stored communications consist of recordings of video calls made or received using an individual message/call application service—disclose to the Organisation:
specified telecommunications data that relates to those video calls; and
specified telecommunications data that relates to the individual message/call application service; and
if the stored communications consist of material that has been uploaded by an end-user for storage or back-up by a storage/back-up service—disclose to the Organisation:
specified telecommunications data that relates to that material; and
specified telecommunications data that relates to the end-user’s account with the storage/back-up service; and
if the stored communications consist of material posted to a general electronic content service by an end-user—disclose to the Organisation:
specified telecommunications data that relates to that material; and
specified telecommunications data that relates to the end-user’s account with the general electronic content service.
Matters to which nominated ART Intelligence and Security member must have regard
In deciding whether to issue an international production order under subclause (2), the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member must have regard to the following matters:

to what extent methods of carrying out the Organisation’s function of obtaining intelligence relating to security (so far as carrying out that function relates to the relevant person) that are less intrusive than obtaining, under such an order, a copy of the stored communications have been used by, or are available to, the Organisation;

how much the use of such methods would be likely to assist the Organisation in carrying out its function of obtaining intelligence relating to security (so far as carrying out that function relates to the relevant person);

how much the use of such methods would be likely to prejudice the Organisation in carrying out its function of obtaining intelligence relating to security (so far as carrying out that function relates to the relevant person);
such other matters (if any) as the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member considers relevant.
Scope
This clause applies to an international production order issued under clause 98.
Content
The order must be signed by the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member who issued it.
The order must set out the following:
the date on which the order was issued;
the name of the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed;
the name of the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order.

If the order directs a prescribed communications provider to make a copy of stored communications available to the Organisation, the order may require the provider to make that copy available to the Organisation in a specified way.
A requirement under subclause (4) may:
require that a copy of stored communications be made available to the Organisation directly; or
require that a copy of stored communications be made available to the Organisation indirectly via the Australian Designated Authority.

If the order directs a prescribed communications provider to disclose telecommunications data to the Organisation, the order may require the provider to disclose that data to the Organisation in a specified way.
A requirement under subclause (6) may:
require that the telecommunications data be disclosed to the Organisation directly; or
require that the telecommunications data be disclosed to the Organisation indirectly via the Australian Designated Authority.
For the purposes of this clause, a specified way may deal with matters of timing.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Issue of further international production order

content.p: If:
(a) an international production order (the original order) was issued under clause 98; and
the original order was in respect of a particular person; and
the original order was directed to a prescribed communications provider;
this Schedule does not prevent the issue of a further international production order under clause 98 that:
is in respect of the person; and
is directed to the provider.

hcontainer.name: division
hcontainer.heading: International production orders relating to telecommunications data: national security

content.p: Subdivision A—Applications

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Application for international production order—national security

content.p: The Organisation may apply to a nominated ART Intelligence and Security member for an international production order under clause 107 that:
is in respect of a particular person; and
is directed to a prescribed communications provider.
The application must nominate a designated international agreement.
The application must be made on the Organisation’s behalf by:
the Director-General of Security; or
a Deputy Director-General of Security; or
an eligible position-holder in relation to whom an authorisation is in force under subclause (4).

The Director-General of Security may authorise in writing, for the purposes of subclause (3), eligible position-holders who, or classes of eligible position-holders who, are entitled under subclause (1) to make applications on the Organisation’s behalf.
An application under clause 101 must be in writing.

If the person making an application under clause 101 for an international production order on the Organisation’s behalf thinks it necessary, because of urgent circumstances, to make the application by telephone, the person may make the application by telephone.
Note: See also clause 17A (urgent circumstances) and clause 172 (action required).
An application under clause 101 must, if it is in writing, set out:
a statement to the effect that the application is made by the Organisation; and
the name of the person making the application on the Organisation’s behalf.
An application under clause 101 must, if it is in writing, be accompanied by an affidavit complying with this clause.
The affidavit must set out the facts and other grounds on which the application is based.

Despite subclause (1), a written application may be accompanied by 2 or more affidavits that together set out each matter that, apart from this subclause, this clause would have required an affidavit accompanying the application to set out.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Information to be given on telephone application

content.p: The information given to a nominated ART Intelligence and Security member in connection with a telephone application under clause 101 to the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member:
must include particulars of the urgent circumstances because of which the person making the application on the Organisation’s behalf thinks it necessary to make the application by telephone; and
must include each matter that, if the application had been made in writing, clause 103 or 104 would have required the application, or an affidavit accompanying it, to set out; and
must be given orally or in writing, as the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member directs.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Giving further information to nominated ART Intelligence and Security member

content.p: A nominated ART Intelligence and Security member may require further information to be given in connection with an application under clause 101 to the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member for an international production order.
The further information:
must be given on oath if the application was made in writing; and
must be given orally or otherwise, as the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member directs.
Subdivision B—International production orders relating to telecommunications data

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Issue of international production order—national security

content.p: Scope
This clause applies if the Organisation applies, under clause 101, to a nominated ART Intelligence and Security member for an international production order that:
(a) is in respect of a particular person (the relevant person); and
is directed to a prescribed communications provider.
Issue of international production order

If the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member is satisfied, on the basis of the information given to the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member under this Division in connection with the application, that:
there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that the prescribed communications provider holds, or is likely to commence to hold, any of the following telecommunications data:
telecommunications data that relates to communications that the relevant person has made using an individual transmission service supplied by the prescribed communications provider;

telecommunications data that relates to an individual transmission service supplied using a telecommunications network owned or operated by the prescribed communications provider, where the individual transmission service is used, or is likely to be used, by the relevant person;

telecommunications data that relates to an individual transmission service supplied by the prescribed communications provider, where the individual transmission service is used, or is likely to be used, by the relevant person;
telecommunications data that relates to messages sent or received by the relevant person using an individual message/call application service provided by the prescribed communications provider;
telecommunications data that relates to voice calls made or received by the relevant person using an individual message/call application service provided by the prescribed communications provider;
telecommunications data that relates to video calls made or received by the relevant person using an individual message/call application service provided by the prescribed communications provider;

telecommunications data that relates to an individual message/call application service provided by the prescribed communications provider, where the individual message/call application service is used, or is likely to be used, by the relevant person;
telecommunications data that relates to material that has been uploaded by the relevant person for storage or back-up by a storage/back-up service provided by the prescribed communications provider;
telecommunications data that relates to material that has been posted by the relevant person on a general electronic content service provided by the prescribed communications provider; and

the person who made the application on behalf of the Organisation reasonably suspects that the prescribed communications provider is based in, or operates in, a foreign country that is a party to the designated international agreement nominated in the application; and
Subdivision A has been complied with in relation to the application; and
in the case of a telephone application—because of urgent circumstances, it was necessary to make the application by telephone; and
disclosing the telecommunications data to the Organisation, under an order issued under this clause, would be in connection with the performance by the Organisation of its functions;

the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member may issue an order (to be known as an international production order) directing the prescribed communications provider to do either or both of the following:

so far as the telecommunications data is held by the prescribed communications provider when the international production order comes into force—disclose any such telecommunications data to the Organisation;
so far as the telecommunications data commences to be held by the prescribed communications provider during a specified period—disclose any such telecommunications data to the Organisation.
Period specified in international production order
A period specified in an international production order for the purposes of paragraph (2)(f) must not begin before the time when the order is given to the prescribed communications provider.
Note: International production orders are given under clause 112.
A period specified in an international production order for the purposes of paragraph (2)(f) must not be longer than 90 days.
Matters to which nominated ART Intelligence and Security member must have regard
In deciding whether to issue an international production order under subclause (2), the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member must have regard to the following matters:

to what extent methods of performing the Organisation’s functions (so far as performing those functions relates to the relevant person) that are less intrusive than obtaining, under such an order, the telecommunications data have been used by, or are available to, the Organisation;
how much the use of such methods would be likely to assist the Organisation in performing its functions (so far as performing those functions relates to the relevant person);

how much the use of such methods would be likely to prejudice the Organisation in performing its functions (so far as performing those functions relates to the relevant person), whether because of delay or for any other reason;
such other matters (if any) as the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member considers relevant.
Scope
This clause applies to an international production order issued under clause 107.
Content
The order must be signed by the nominated ART Intelligence and Security member who issued it.
The order must set out the following:
the date on which the order was issued;
the name of the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed;
the name of the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order.

If the order directs a prescribed communications provider to disclose telecommunications data to the Organisation, the order may require the provider to disclose that data to the Organisation in a specified way.
A requirement under subclause (4) may:
require that the telecommunications data be disclosed to the Organisation directly; or
require that the telecommunications data be disclosed to the Organisation indirectly via the Australian Designated Authority.
For the purposes of this clause, a specified way may deal with matters of timing.

Example: If a requirement under subclause (4) relates to telecommunications data that commences to be held by a prescribed communications provider during a specified period, the requirement may require that the telecommunications data be disclosed to the Organisation within 30 minutes after the telecommunications data commences to be held.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Issue of further international production order

content.p: If:
(a) an international production order (the original order) was issued under clause 107; and
the original order was in respect of a particular person; and
the original order was directed to a prescribed communications provider;
this Schedule does not prevent the issue of a further international production order under clause 107 that:
is in respect of the person; and
is directed to the provider.

• Before an international production order is given to a prescribed communications provider, the Australian Designated Authority must consider whether the order complies with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order.

• If the Australian Designated Authority is satisfied that the order complies with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order, the Australian Designated Authority must give the order to the prescribed communications provider. The order comes in force when it is given to the provider.

• If the Australian Designated Authority is not satisfied that the order complies with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order, the Australian Designated Authority must cancel the order.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Giving of international production orders—relevant agency

content.p: If an international production order is issued under Part 2 or 3 of this Schedule:
the relevant agency that applied for the order must:
give the order, or a certified copy of the order, to the Australian Designated Authority; and
do so as soon as practicable after the order is issued; and
the Australian Designated Authority must consider whether the order complies with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order; and

if the Australian Designated Authority is satisfied that the order complies with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order—the Australian Designated Authority must:
give the order, or the certified copy of the order, to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed; and
do so as soon as practicable after becoming so satisfied; and

if the Australian Designated Authority is not satisfied that the order complies with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order—the Australian Designated Authority must:
cancel the order; and
return the order, or the certified copy of the order, to the agency; and
give the agency such advice as the Australian Designated Authority considers appropriate in relation to compliance with the designated international agreement.
Note: See clause 171 (which deals with electronic service of documents).

For the purposes of this Schedule, if the Australian Designated Authority gives a certified copy of an international production order to a prescribed communications provider under subclause (1), the Australian Designated Authority is taken to have given the order to the prescribed communications provider under subclause (1).
An international production order issued under Part 2 or 3 of this Schedule comes into force when it is given to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed.

For the purposes of this Schedule, if the Australian Designated Authority gives an international production order to a prescribed communications provider under subclause (1), the order is taken to invoke the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order.

If the Australian Designated Authority gives an international production order to a prescribed communications provider under subclause (1), the Australian Designated Authority must notify the giving of the order to the relevant agency that applied for the order.
A cancellation under paragraph (1)(d) is to be set out in a written instrument.

If an international production order is issued under Part 2 or 3 of this Schedule, the relevant agency that applied for the order may give the Australian Designated Authority information that is likely to assist the Australian Designated Authority in making a decision under this clause in relation to the order.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Giving of international production orders—the Organisation

content.p: If an international production order is issued under Part 4 of this Schedule:
the Organisation must:
give the order, or a certified copy of the order, to the Australian Designated Authority; and
do so as soon as practicable after the order is issued; and
the Australian Designated Authority must consider whether the order complies with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order; and

if the Australian Designated Authority is satisfied that the order complies with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order—the Australian Designated Authority must:
give the order, or the certified copy of the order, to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed; and
do so as soon as practicable after becoming so satisfied; and

if the Australian Designated Authority is not satisfied that the order complies with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order—the Australian Designated Authority must:
cancel the order; and
return the order, or the certified copy of the order, to the Organisation; and
give the Organisation such advice as the Australian Designated Authority considers appropriate in relation to compliance with the designated international agreement.
Note: See clause 171 (which deals with electronic service of documents).

For the purposes of this Schedule, if the Australian Designated Authority gives a certified copy of an international production order to a prescribed communications provider under subclause (1), the Australian Designated Authority is taken to have given the order to the prescribed communications provider under subclause (1).
An international production order issued under Part 4 of this Schedule comes into force when it is given to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed.

For the purposes of this Schedule, if the Australian Designated Authority gives an international production order to a prescribed communications provider under subclause (1), the order is taken to invoke the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order.

If the Australian Designated Authority gives an international production order to a prescribed communications provider under subclause (1), the Australian Designated Authority must notify the giving of the order to the Organisation.
A cancellation under paragraph (1)(d) is to be set out in a written instrument.

If an international production order is issued under Part 4 of this Schedule, the Organisation may give the Australian Designated Authority information that is likely to assist the Australian Designated Authority in making a decision under this clause in relation to the order.
• If an international production order was issued in response to an application made by a relevant agency, the chief officer of the agency:
may revoke the order; and
must revoke the order if the chief officer is satisfied that the grounds on which the order was issued have ceased to exist.
• If an international production order was issued in response to an application made by the Organisation, the Director-General of Security:
may revoke the order; and
must revoke the order if the Director-General of Security is satisfied that the grounds on which the order was issued have ceased to exist.

• If an international production order is revoked after it has come into force, the Australian Designated Authority must give the instrument of revocation to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Revocation of international production orders—relevant agency

content.p: If:
an international production order was issued under Part 2 or 3 of this Schedule; and
the order was issued in response to an application made by a relevant agency;
the chief officer of the agency:
may revoke the order; and
must revoke the order if the chief officer is satisfied that the grounds on which the order was issued have ceased to exist.
A revocation under this clause is to be set out in a written instrument.

For the purposes of the application of subclause (1) to an international production order issued under Part 3 of this Schedule on the ground that a Part 5.3 supervisory order was in force in relation to a particular person when the international production order was issued, that ground is taken to have ceased to exist if, and only if, neither that Part 5.3 supervisory order, nor any succeeding Part 5.3 supervisory order, is in force.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Giving of instrument of revocation—relevant agency

content.p: If an international production order is revoked under clause 114 by the chief officer of a relevant agency, the relevant agency must:
give the instrument of revocation to the Australian Designated Authority; and
do so as soon as practicable after the order is revoked.
If:
the Australian Designated Authority gave an international production order to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed; and
the order was subsequently revoked under clause 114;
the Australian Designated Authority must:
give the instrument of revocation to the prescribed communications provider; and
do so as soon as practicable after the instrument of revocation is given to the Australian Designated Authority.
A revocation under clause 114 takes effect:
if the instrument of revocation is required to be given to the prescribed communications provider concerned—when the instrument is given; or
otherwise—when the revocation is made.
If:
an international production order is revoked under clause 114; and
when the revocation takes effect, the Australian Designated Authority has not made a decision about the order under clause 111;
clause 111 ceases to apply to the order when the revocation takes effect.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Revocation of international production orders—the Organisation

content.p: If an international production order was issued under Part 4 of this Schedule, the Director-General of Security:
may revoke the order; and
must revoke the order if the Director-General of Security is satisfied that the grounds on which the order was issued have ceased to exist.
A revocation under this clause is to be set out in a written instrument.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Giving of instrument of revocation—the Organisation

content.p: If an international production order is revoked under clause 116 by the Director-General of Security, the Organisation must:
give the instrument of revocation to the Australian Designated Authority; and
do so as soon as practicable after the order is revoked.
If:
the Australian Designated Authority gave an international production order to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed; and
the order was subsequently revoked under clause 116;
the Australian Designated Authority must:
give the instrument of revocation to the prescribed communications provider; and
do so as soon as practicable after the instrument of revocation is given to the Australian Designated Authority.
A revocation under clause 116 takes effect:
if the instrument of revocation is required to be given to the prescribed communications provider concerned—when the instrument is given; or
otherwise—when the revocation is made.
If:
an international production order is revoked under clause 116; and
when the revocation takes effect, the Australian Designated Authority has not made a decision about the order under clause 112;
clause 112 ceases to apply to the order when the revocation takes effect.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Delegation by the chief officer of a relevant agency

content.p: The chief officer of a relevant agency may, by writing, delegate any or all of the chief officer’s functions or powers under this Part to a certifying officer of the agency.
In performing functions, or exercising powers, under a delegation under subclause (1), the delegate must comply with any directions of the chief officer.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Delegation by the Director-General of Security

content.p: The Director-General of Security may, by writing, delegate any or all of the Director-General of Security’s functions or powers under this Part to a person who is:
a Deputy Director-General of Security; or
an ASIO employee.
In performing functions, or exercising powers, under a delegation under subclause (1), the delegate must comply with any directions of the Director-General of Security.

hcontainer.name: part
hcontainer.heading: Objections to, and cancellation of, international production orders

content.p: • If an international production order is given to a prescribed communications provider, the provider may object to the order on the grounds that the order does not comply with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order.
• The Australian Designated Authority may cancel an international production order.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Prescribed communications provider may object to international production order

content.p: If an international production order is given to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed, the provider may, by written notice given to the Australian Designated Authority, object to the order on the grounds that the order does not comply with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order.
The notice must:
be given to the Australian Designated Authority within a reasonable time after the international production order is given to the prescribed communications provider; and
set out the reasons why the provider considers that the order does not comply with the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order.
The Australian Designated Authority may cancel an international production order.
A cancellation under subclause (1) is to be set out in a written instrument.
If an international production order is cancelled under subclause (1), the Australian Designated Authority must:
if the order was issued under Part 2 or 3 of this Schedule in response to an application by a relevant agency:
inform the chief officer of the relevant agency of the cancellation; and
do so as soon as practicable after cancelling the order; or
if the order was issued under Part 4 of this Schedule:
inform the Organisation of the cancellation; and
do so as soon as practicable after cancelling the order.
If:
the Australian Designated Authority gave an international production order to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed; and
the order was subsequently cancelled under subclause (1);
the Australian Designated Authority must:
give the instrument of cancellation to the prescribed communications provider; and
do so as soon as practicable after cancelling the order.
A cancellation under subclause (1) takes effect:
if the instrument of cancellation is required to be given to the prescribed communications provider concerned—when the instrument is given; or
otherwise—when the cancellation is made.
If:
an international production order is cancelled under this clause; and
when the cancellation takes effect, the Australian Designated Authority has not made a decision about the order under clause 111 or 112 (as the case may be);
clause 111 or 112 (as the case may be) ceases to apply to the order when the cancellation takes effect.
• Civil penalties apply for failing to comply with international production orders.
If:
an international production order is given to the prescribed communications provider to whom the order is directed; and
the order is in force; and
when the order is given, the prescribed communications provider meets the enforcement threshold;
the prescribed communications provider must comply with the order to the extent to which the prescribed communications provider is capable of doing so.
Civil penalty: 238 penalty units.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: When a prescribed communications provider meets the enforcement threshold

content.p: For the purposes of this Schedule, if:
a prescribed communications provider owns or operates a telecommunications network that is used to supply a transmission service to one or more Australians; or
a prescribed communications provider supplies a transmission service to one or more Australians; or
a prescribed communications provider provides a message/call application service to one or more Australians; or
a prescribed communications provider provides a storage/back-up service to one or more Australians; or
one or more Australians have posted material on a general electronic content service provided by a prescribed communications provider;
the prescribed communications provider meets the enforcement threshold unless:

if paragraph (a) applies—the provider of a transmission service supplied using the telecommunications network cannot reasonably be considered to have offered or provided the transmission service on the basis of the service being available to Australians; and

if paragraph (b) applies—the prescribed communications provider cannot reasonably be considered to have offered or provided the transmission service on the basis of the service being available to Australians; and

if paragraph (c) applies—the prescribed communications provider cannot reasonably be considered to have offered or provided the message/call application service on the basis of the service being available to Australians; and

if paragraph (d) applies—the prescribed communications provider cannot reasonably be considered to have offered or provided the storage/back-up service on the basis of the service being available to Australians; and

if paragraph (e) applies—the prescribed communications provider cannot reasonably be considered to have offered or provided the general electronic content service on the basis of the opportunity to post material on the service being available to Australians.
Australian
(2) For the purposes of this clause, Australian means an individual who is ordinarily resident in Australia.
Enforceable civil penalty provision
(1) A civil penalty provision in this Part is enforceable under Part 4 of the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Act 2014.

Note: Part 4 of the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Act 2014 allows a civil penalty provision to be enforced by obtaining an order for a person to pay a pecuniary penalty for the contravention of the provision.
Authorised applicant

(2) For the purposes of Part 4 of the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Act 2014, a Communications Access Coordinator is an authorised applicant in relation to a civil penalty provision in this Part.
Relevant court

(3) For the purposes of Part 4 of the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Act 2014, the Federal Court of Australia and the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia are relevant courts in relation to a civil penalty provision in this Part.
Penalty for a body corporate

(4) Paragraph 82(5)(a) of the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Act 2014, as it applies in relation to a civil penalty provision in this Part, has effect as if “5 times” were omitted and “200 times” were substituted.
Extra-territorial application

(5) Part 4 of the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Act 2014, as it applies in relation to a civil penalty provision in this Part, extends to acts, omissions, matters and things outside Australia.
• The chief officer of a relevant agency and the Australian Designated Authority must give the Minister annual reports about matters relating to international production orders.

• The Director-General of Security must give the Attorney-General a report on the extent to which compliance by a prescribed communications provider with an international production order has assisted the Organisation in carrying out its functions.
• The Minister must cause to be prepared annual reports about matters relating to international production orders that were issued in response to applications made by relevant agencies.

• The chief officer of a relevant agency, the Director-General of Security and the Australian Designated Authority must ensure that records are kept of matters relating to international production orders.
The chief officer of a relevant agency must, within 3 months after the end of each financial year, give the Minister a written report that sets out:
the relevant statistics about applications made by the agency under clause 22 during the financial year; and
the relevant statistics about applications made by the agency under clause 33 during the financial year; and
the relevant statistics about applications made by the agency under clause 42 during the financial year; and
the relevant statistics about applications made by the agency under clause 52 during the financial year; and
the relevant statistics about applications made by the agency under clause 63 during the financial year; and
the relevant statistics about applications made by the agency under clause 72 during the financial year; and

for each designated international agreement—the number of applications made by the agency under Part 2 or 3 of this Schedule during the financial year that nominated the designated international agreement; and
if one or more international production orders were issued before the end of the financial year in response to applications made by the agency:
the number of occasions during the financial year on which protected information obtained in accordance with those orders was shared with other relevant agencies; and
the number of arrests that were made during the financial year on the basis of protected information obtained in accordance with those orders; and
the number of prosecutions where protected information obtained in accordance with those orders was used in evidence during the financial year; and

the number of convictions during the financial year where protected information obtained in accordance with those orders was used in evidence in the prosecutions that resulted in those convictions; and

if one or more international production orders were issued under clause 30 during the financial year, in response to applications made by the agency, on grounds relating to the investigation of one or more offences—the type or types of those offences; and

if one or more international production orders were issued under clause 39 during the financial year, in response to applications made by the agency, on grounds relating to the investigation of one or more offences—the type or types of those offences; and

if one or more international production orders were issued under clause 48 during the financial year, in response to applications made by the agency, on grounds relating to the investigation of one or more offences—the type or types of those offences; and
the number of international production orders revoked by the chief officer under clause 114 during the financial year; and

if subparagraph 30(2)(g)(ii) or (h)(ii) applied to one or more international production orders issued under clause 30 during the financial year in response to applications made by the agency—the number of those orders; and

if subparagraph 60(2)(g)(ii) or (h)(ii) applied to one or more international production orders issued under clause 60 during the financial year in response to applications made by the agency—the number of those orders.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Reports to be made to the Attorney-General by the Director-General of Security

content.p: The Director-General of Security must:

give the Attorney-General, in respect of each international production order issued under clause 89, a written report on the extent to which compliance by a prescribed communications provider with the order has assisted the Organisation in carrying out its functions; and
do so within 3 months after whichever of the following first occurs:
the end of the last day on which the prescribed communications provider could have done an act or thing in compliance with the order;
the time when the order ceases to be in force because of the revocation or cancellation of the order.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Annual reports by the Australian Designated Authority

content.p: The Australian Designated Authority must, within 3 months after the end of each financial year, give the Minister a written report that sets out, for each relevant agency:

if one or more international production orders issued in response to applications made by the agency were given by the Australian Designated Authority to prescribed communications providers during the financial year:
the number of those orders; and
the number of each type of those orders; and
for each designated international agreement—the number of those orders that invoked the designated international agreement; and
if subparagraph 30(2)(g)(ii) or (h)(ii) applied to one or more international production orders that were:
issued under clause 30 in response to applications made by the agency; and
given by the Australian Designated Authority to prescribed communications providers during the financial year;
the number of those orders; and
if subparagraph 60(2)(g)(ii) or (h)(ii) applied to one or more international production orders that were:
issued under clause 60 in response to applications made by the agency; and
given by the Australian Designated Authority to prescribed communications providers during the financial year;
the number of those orders; and

if one or more international production orders issued in response to applications made by the agency were cancelled by the Australian Designated Authority under clause 111 during the financial year—the number of those orders; and

if one or more international production orders issued in response to applications made by the agency were cancelled by the Australian Designated Authority under clause 122 during the financial year—the number of those orders; and

if one or more instruments of revocation of international production orders issued in response to applications made by the agency were given by the Australian Designated Authority to prescribed communications providers during the financial year—the number of those instruments; and

if one or more objections were received by the Australian Designated Authority under clause 121 during the financial year in relation to international production orders issued in response to applications made by the agency:
the number of international production orders to which those objections relate; and
the number of each type of those orders; and
for each designated international agreement—the number of those orders that invoked the designated international agreement.
The Minister must:
cause a copy of a report under subclause (1) to be given to the Attorney-General; and
do so as soon as practicable after receiving the report.
The Minister must, as soon as practicable after the end of each financial year, cause to be prepared a written report that:
sets out, for each relevant agency, the information contained in the report by the chief officer of the agency under clause 128 for the financial year; and
sets out the information contained in the report by the Australian Designated Authority under clause 130 for the financial year.
Report to be tabled
The Minister must cause a copy of a report under subclause (1) to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the report is prepared.
A report under subclause (1) must not be made in a manner that is likely to enable the identification of a person.

(4) For the purposes of section 34C of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901, a report that subclause (1) requires to be prepared as soon as practicable after the end of a financial year is taken to be a periodic report that this Act requires a person to furnish to the Minister and that relates to the administration of this Schedule during the financial year.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Deferral of inclusion of information in Ministerial report

content.p: Scope
This clause applies to information:
included in a report given to the Minister:
under clause 128 by the chief officer of a relevant agency; or
under clause 130 by the Australian Designated Authority; and
that the Minister would, apart from this clause, be required to include in the next Ministerial report.
Exclusion of information—relevant agency
If:
subparagraph (1)(a)(i) applies; and
the chief officer of the relevant agency is satisfied that the information is Part 5.3 information;
the chief officer must advise the Minister in writing not to include the information in the next Ministerial report.
If the Minister is satisfied, on the advice of the chief officer, that the information is Part 5.3 information, the Minister must:
notify the chief officer in writing; and
not include the information in any Ministerial report until the Minister decides otherwise under subclause (5).
Inclusion of information in subsequent report—relevant agency
If the information has not been included in a Ministerial report because of subclause (3), the chief officer must, before the Minister prepares the next Ministerial report:
reconsider whether the information is Part 5.3 information; and
if the chief officer is satisfied that the information is not Part 5.3 information—advise the Minister in writing to include the information in the next Ministerial report.
If the Minister is satisfied, on the advice of the chief officer, that the information is not Part 5.3 information, the Minister must:
notify the chief officer in writing; and
include the information in the next Ministerial report.
Exclusion of information—Australian Designated Authority
If:
subparagraph (1)(a)(ii) applies; and
the Australian Designated Authority is satisfied that the information is Part 5.3 information;
the Australian Designated Authority must advise the Minister in writing not to include the information in the next Ministerial report.
If the Minister is satisfied, on the advice of the Australian Designated Authority, that the information is Part 5.3 information, the Minister must:
notify the Australian Designated Authority in writing; and
not include the information in any Ministerial report until the Minister decides otherwise under subclause (9).
Inclusion of information in subsequent report—Australian Designated Authority
If the information has not been included in a Ministerial report because of subclause (7), the Australian Designated Authority must, before the Minister prepares the next Ministerial report:
reconsider whether the information is Part 5.3 information; and
if the Australian Designated Authority is satisfied that the information is not Part 5.3 information—advise the Minister in writing to include the information in the next Ministerial report.
If the Minister is satisfied, on the advice of the Australian Designated Authority, that the information is not Part 5.3 information, the Minister must:
notify the chief officer in writing; and
include the information in the next Ministerial report.
Definitions
In this clause:
Ministerial report means a report the Minister causes to be prepared under clause 131.
Part 5.3 information means information that, if made public, could reasonably be expected to enable a reasonable person to conclude that:
an international production order is likely to be, or is not likely to be, in force under Part 3 of this Schedule in relation to:
an individual carriage service used, or likely to be used, by a particular person; or
an individual message/call application service used, or likely to be used, by a particular person; or
stored communications that consist of communications that a particular person has made has made using an individual carriage service; or
stored communications that consist of messages that a particular person has sent or received using an individual message/call application service; or
stored communications that consist of recordings of voice calls that a particular person has made or received using an individual message/call application service; or
stored communications that consist of recordings of video calls that a particular person has made or received using an individual message/call application service; or
stored communications that consist of material that a particular person has uploaded for storage or back-up by a storage/back-up service; or
stored communications that consist of material that a particular person has posted to a general electronic content service; or
telecommunications data that relates to communications that a particular person has made using an individual carriage service; or
telecommunications data that relates to an individual carriage service used, or likely to be used, by a particular person; or
telecommunications data that relates to messages sent or received by a particular person using an individual message/call application service; or
telecommunications data that relates to voice calls made or received by a particular person using an individual message/call application service; or
telecommunications data that relates to video calls made or received by a particular person using an individual message/call application service; or
telecommunications data that relates to an individual message/call application service used, or likely to be used, by a particular person; or
telecommunications data that relates to material that has been uploaded by a particular person for storage or back-up by a storage/back-up service; or
telecommunications data that relates to material that has been posted by a particular person on a general electronic content service; or
an international production order is likely to be, or is not likely to be, in force under Part 3 of this Schedule in relation to a particular person.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Keeping documents associated with international production orders—relevant agencies

content.p: The chief officer of a relevant agency must cause the following to be kept in the agency’s records:
a copy of each written application made by the agency for an international production order;
a copy of each affidavit that accompanied a written application made by the agency for an international production order;
a copy of each international production order issued in response to an application made by the agency;
a copy of each authorisation given by the chief officer under subclause 23(3);
a copy of each authorisation given by the chief officer under subclause 34(3);
a copy of each authorisation given by the chief officer under subclause 43(3);
a copy of each authorisation given by the chief officer under subclause 53(3);
a copy of each authorisation given by the chief officer under subclause 64(3);
a copy of each authorisation given by the chief officer under subclause 73(3);
if the chief officer revokes an international production order under clause 114—a copy of the instrument of revocation.
The period for which the chief officer of a relevant agency must cause a copy of a particular document to be kept in the agency’s records under subclause (1) is the period:
starting when the document came into existence; and
ending:
when 3 years have elapsed since the document came into existence; or
if the Ombudsman is required to give a report to the Minister under clause 150 that is about records that include the copy—when the Ombudsman gives the report;
whichever happens earlier.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Other records to be kept—relevant agencies

content.p: The chief officer of a relevant agency must cause the following to be kept in the agency’s records:
details of each telephone application made by the agency for an international production order;
for each application made by the agency for an international production order—a statement as to whether the application was granted, refused or withdrawn;
for each international production order issued in response to an application made by the agency:
a record of the type of order; and
a record of the designated international agreement nominated in the application; and
a statement as to whether the international production order was issued on grounds relating to the investigation of one or more offences and, if so, the type or types of those offences; and
if subparagraph 30(2)(g)(ii) or (h)(ii) applied to the order—a statement to that effect; and
if subparagraph 60(2)(g)(ii) or (h)(ii) applied to the order—a statement to that effect; and
if a period was specified in the order—details of that period; and
a record of the agency giving the order, or a certified copy of the order, to the Australian Designated Authority; and
details of each communication by an officer of the agency to a person other than an officer of the agency of protected information obtained in accordance with the order; and
a record of the prescribed communications provider to whom the order was directed; and
a statement as to whether the prescribed communications provider complied with the order; and
if the prescribed communications provider made intercepted communications, messages, voice calls or video calls available to the agency directly—a statement to that effect; and
if the prescribed communications provider made stored communications or telecommunications data available to the agency directly—a statement to that effect; and
if the agency used protected information obtained in accordance with the order—a statement setting out details of that use of the protected information; and
if the chief officer revoked the order under clause 114—a statement setting out the reasons for the revocation; and
if the Australian Designated Authority cancelled the order under clause 122—a record of the cancellation; and
if a certifying officer of the agency certified a document to be a true copy of the order—a statement to that effect;
documents indicating whether a record was destroyed in accordance with subclause 140(1) or (3);
documents and other materials of a kind prescribed under subclause (2).
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, prescribe kinds of documents and other materials that the chief officer of a relevant agency must cause to be kept in the agency’s records.
The period for which the chief officer of a relevant agency must cause a particular item to be kept in the agency’s records under subclause (1) is the period:
starting when the item came into existence; and
ending:
when 3 years have elapsed since the item came into existence; or
if the Ombudsman is required to give a report to the Minister under clause 150 that is about records that include the copy—when the Ombudsman gives the report;
whichever happens earlier.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Keeping documents associated with international production orders—the Organisation

content.p: The Director-General of Security must cause the following to be kept in the Organisation’s records:
a copy of each written application made under Part 4 of this Schedule for an international production order;
a copy of each affidavit that accompanied a written application under Part 4 of this Schedule for an international production order;
a copy of each written request that the Attorney-General consent orally to the making of an application under Part 4 of this Schedule for an international production order;
a copy of each written consent by the Attorney-General to the making of an application under Part 4 of this Schedule for an international production order;
a copy of each report given to the Attorney-General under subclause 83(9) or 92(9);
a copy of each document of a kind specified in a written agreement between the Director-General of Security and the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security;
a copy of each international production order issued under Part 4 of this Schedule;
a copy of each authorisation given by the Director-General of Security under subclause 83(4);
a copy of each authorisation given by the Director-General of Security under subclause 92(4);
a copy of each authorisation given by the Director-General of Security under subclause 101(4);
if the Director-General of Security revoked an international production order under clause 116—a copy of the instrument of revocation.
The period for which the Director-General of Security must cause a copy of a particular document to be kept in the Organisation’s records under subclause (1) is the period:
starting when the document came into existence; and
if:
the document relates to an international production order that was issued under Part 4 of this Schedule; and
information was obtained in accordance with the order;
ending at the later of the following times:
when 3 years have elapsed since the document came into existence;
when the Organisation ceases to retain the information that was obtained in accordance with the order; and
if paragraph (b) does not apply—ending when 3 years have elapsed since the document came into existence.
An agreement under paragraph (1)(bd) is not a legislative instrument.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Other records to be kept—the Organisation

content.p: The Director-General of Security must cause the following to be kept in the Organisation’s records:
details of each telephone application made under Part 4 of this Schedule for an international production order;
for each application made under Part 4 of this Schedule for an international production order—a statement as to whether the application was granted, refused or withdrawn;
a record of each oral request that the Attorney-General consent orally to the making of an application under Part 4 of this Schedule for an international production order;
a record of each oral consent by the Attorney-General to the making of an application under Part 4 of this Schedule for an international production order;
each record of a kind specified in a written agreement between the Director-General of Security and the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security;
for each international production order issued under Part 4 of this Schedule:
a record of the type of order; and
a record of the designated international agreement nominated in the application for the order; and
if a period was specified in the order—details of that period; and
a record of the Organisation giving the order, or a certified copy of the order, to the Australian Designated Authority; and
details of each communication by an ASIO official to a person other than an ASIO official of protected information obtained in accordance with the order; and
a record of the prescribed communications provider to whom the order was directed; and
a statement as to whether the prescribed communications provider complied with the order; and

if the prescribed communications provider made intercepted communications, messages, voice calls, video calls, stored communications or telecommunications data available to the Organisation directly—a statement to that effect; and
if the Organisation used protected information obtained in accordance with the order—a statement setting out details of that use of the protected information; and
if the Director-General of Security revokes the order under clause 116—a statement setting out the reasons for the revocation; and
if the Australian Designated Authority cancelled the order under clause 122—a record of the cancellation; and
if a certifying person certified a document to be a true copy of the order—a statement to that effect;
documents indicating whether a record was destroyed in accordance with subclause 140(2) or (4).
The period for which the Director-General of Security must cause a particular record to be kept in the Organisation’s records under subclause (1) is the period:
starting when the record came into existence; and
if:
the record relates to an international production order that was issued under Part 4 of this Schedule; and
information was obtained in accordance with the order;
ending at the later of the following times:
when 3 years have elapsed since the record came into existence;
when the Organisation ceases to retain the information that was obtained in accordance with the order; and
if paragraph (b) does not apply—ending when 3 years have elapsed since the record came into existence.
An agreement under paragraph (1)(bc) is not a legislative instrument.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Keeping documents associated with international production orders—Australian Designated Authority

content.p: The Australian Designated authority must cause the following to be kept in the Australian Designated Authority’s records:
